Court No. - 15

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 536 of 2024
Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Kripa Shankar Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.
Heard Shri Shashindra Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
Learned A.G.A. informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter including up-to-date case diary and charge sheet has also been submitted.

2. The instant application has been moved by the applicant- Pradeep Kumar in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 309 of 2021, under Sections 420, 406, 504 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station Bangarmau, District Unnao, with the prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail, as he is apprehending arrest in the above-mentioned case.
3. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the anticipatory bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.

While drawing the attention of this Court towards a Pradeep Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ... on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177817109/
1 partnership-deed, a copy of which has been placed at Annexure No.1 to the affidavit, it is alleged that the dispute between the parties is pertaining to the non-payment of some money which were allegedly invested by the informant.

4. It is vehemently submitted that the amount of investment is shown to have been given in cash,
which is patently false and could not be believed as an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/- may not be paid in cash and there is no evidence that the same has been withdrawn by the informant from the bank on any date close to the date on which it is shown to have been given to the applicant.
5.

It is further submitted that the charged offences against the applicant are punishable with upto seven years' of imprisonment and the applicant has cooperated throughout with the investigation and there was no occasion or opportunity with the investigation officer to have arrested him and since the charge sheet has been filed without arresting him, he is apprehending that when he will appear before the trial court for the purpose of procuring regular bail, the disposal of his bail application may take sometime and in the meantime he may be confined in prison.
6.
It is next submitted that the applicant has not been arrested by the police but is having a serious apprehension of being arrested by the Court, which is required at all.

7. Attention of this Court has also been towards the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 'Mahdoom Bava vs. C.B.I. passed in Criminal Appeal No. Nil of 2023, (arising out of S.L.P. (Crl.) No.
376 of 2023) of date 20.03.2023, Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and others : (2021) 10 SCC 773 and in Aman Preet Singh Vs. C.B.I. through Director : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 941.
8.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that apart from the instant case, the applicant is also shown involved in one other case.
However, the said case has also been instituted by the complainant/informant of this case.

It is undertaken that applicant shall remain present before the trial court as and when his presence would be required and cooperate in the trial, as he has cooperated in the investigation and would not seek any adjournment especially when the prosecution witnesses would be in attendance.
9.

Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of anticipatory bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
10.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, keeping in view the written partnership deed, a copy of which has been placed as Annexure No.1, it appears to be a dispute between the partners of a partnership firm.

Though, learned counsel for the applicant has categorically denied that any money was invested by the informant, however, even if the allegations of the informant as are emerging from the first information report are taken on its face, even then it appears to be a civil dispute.
The charge sheet has been filed without arresting the applicant.
Since the applicant has not been arrested by the investigating agency, I do not find any ground as to why he must be relegated to prison only for disposal of his regular bail application.

12.

sentences.text:
Thus, the instant anticipatory bail application moved by the applicant- Pradeep Kumar is allowed and it is provided that in the event of arrest of the applicant under any process of the trial court or on his appearance before trial court within 20 days from today i.e. till 04.04.2024,
whichever is earlier, he shall be released forthwith on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the S.H.O.
concerned/Investigating/Arresting officer/Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
(i).
The applicant if not arrested earlier, shall surrender before the trial court within 20 days from today and will cooperate in the trial.

(ii). The applicant shall Cooperate in the investigation and will make himself available as and when required by the Investigating officer of the case, even for the recovery of any fact, in case of further investigation.
(iii). The applicant shall not make any attempt to influence the prosecution witnesses and will also not commit any crime during his release on anticipatory bail.
(iv). The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence and specially when the prosecution witnesses are present in court.

(v). The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
13.

If in the opinion of the trial court default of any of the condition placed above is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and shall proceed against him in accordance with law.
14. It is clarified that all the observations contained in this order are only for disposal of this anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial proceedings in any manner.
